summary: Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Lviv (~1919–1924). He worked at the University of Lviv (~1928–1939), Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń (~1945–1953), and headed Indology at the University of Warsaw (~1953–1971).

Eugène Burnouf worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies after studying under Antoine-Léonard Chézy (~1822–1832). He served at the Société Asiatique (1826, 1829, 1832), the Imprimerie Nationale (~1832–1852), and the Collège de France (1832–1852).
Eugène Jacquet was an Indologist and linguist. He studied under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat (~1828–1832) and Eugène Burnouf (~1832–1838).

Eugène Tisserant specialized in history, archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at the Lycée Notre-Dame Saint-Sigisbert, the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~1905–1908), and the École du Louvre (~1905–1908).

Eun Hino is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies who earned a master's degree at the University of Tokyo (~2004–2006). Hino held posts at the University of Tokyo (~2011–2014) and Musashino University (~2014–2018; ~2018).
Eun Maeda was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as president of Toyo University and president of Ryukoku University.

Eun-su Cho, a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, completed a PhD at the University of California, Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini (attested 1997). Cho taught at the University of Michigan until 2004 and joined Seoul National University in 2004.
Eun-young Choi is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at Korea University. Choi held a professorship at Geumgang University, attested from 2013 to 2015.

Eva K. Neumaier is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Khenpo Rigzin. Neumaier held positions at the University of Calgary (attested 1992, 2006) and served as Professor Emeritus, Chair, and Professor at the University of Alberta (attested 2006).

Eva Tichy, a linguist and Indologist, earned her Dr. phil. under Karl Hoffmann at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1974–1981) and habilitated at the University of Marburg (~1982–1989). She held the chair of Indo-European linguistics at the University of Freiburg (1993–2017).

Eva Wilden is an Indologist who completed her MA (~1986–1992), doctorate (~1992–1996), and habilitation (~1997–2004) at the University of Hamburg. She worked at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (2003) and became a professor at the University of Hamburg (2017).

Evan Thompson is a philosopher and religious studies scholar who studied at Amherst College under Robert A. F. Thurman and earned a PhD at the University of Toronto under Francisco J. Varela. He held professorships at York, Toronto, and British Columbia.

Evgenij Ivanovich Kychanov worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of St. Petersburg (~1950–1955) and headed the St. Petersburg branch of the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts in 2002.

Eviatar Shulman is an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~2000–2008). In 2009, he became chairman of the department of comparative religion there.

Eyal Aviv works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He completed a PhD at Harvard University under Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil (attested 2008) and held a post at George Washington University in 2014.

F. B. J. Kuiper, an Indologist and linguist, studied at Utrecht and Leiden (PhD 1934) under Caland, Uhlenbeck, and van Wijk. He taught at Lyceum der Carpentier Alting-Stichting (~1934–1939) and was professor and Kern Institute director at Leiden (1939–1972).

Fa Qing is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He completed his dissertation at the University of Calgary (attested 2001), where he studied under Leslie S. Kawamura, interim supervisor A. W. Barber, and Xiaojie Yang.

Fabienne Jagou is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. She earned a PhD at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences studying under Pierre-Étienne Will, and became a maître de conférences at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~2001).

Fabio Rambelli is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Ca' Foscari, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, and Naples, later holding posts at Sapporo University (2001–2002) and the University of California, Santa Barbara (~2009).

Fabrizia Baldissera is an Indologist who studied at the "Federigo Enriques" Department of Mathematics (1969–2004). She held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~1998) and the University of Florence (attested 2001–2016).
